canonical_digest.json: Compact JSON with lexicographically sorted object keys, preserved array order, and ASCII escaping.
canonical_digest.text_normalization: CRLF and CR become LF; no trimming is applied.

record_content_digest.array_order: Preserve fields, sections, and connections order.

impact_digest.array_order: Preserve outgoing connection and incoming reference order.

diff_digest.array_order: Preserve every card, transition, and source-change order.

proposal_payload_digest.array_order: Preserve every nested array order; duplicated compatibility projections remain included and must agree.

rules: impact_digest equals editor_diff.impact_digest and impact_binding.impact_digest when a removal impact exists.
Every record_document.content_digest and record binding record_digest names the digest of its corresponding record projection.

rules.rule: The server recomputes each supplied digest from its declared canonical projection before accepting it; on idempotency replay it recomputes operation_request.payload_digest before comparing it with the stored receipt.

Every digest uses the exact source, include_fields, exclude_fields, normalization paths, encoding, and array-order rules in digest_projections. Self-referential digest fields are excluded only where named; all duplicated digest fields must agree with their authoritative projection.
Every record document rejects duplicate field_id, section_id, and connection_id values even when the complete objects differ.
Proposal changes, diff cards, authority and visibility entries, references, resolutions, and record bindings are unique by their logical identifiers, not by whole-object equality.

Every record document, including record views and every card before/after document, derives authority from status: canon maps to canon, revealed maps to revealed, every other supported status maps to preparation, and missing or unknown read statuses map to preparation and must be replaced with a supported status before mutation.

Every editor record document and server-produced source snapshot is campaign-owned. The renderer derives ownership as campaign from the campaign revision; clients cannot submit shared or another ownership value to bypass adapter required-field, required-value, nonempty-field, or forbidden-heading validation.

draft, needs_review, rejected, and conflict proposals are not_published with no published revision; approving may be quarantined or not_published with no revision; only approved proposals are published and carry a published revision.

historical is true exactly when viewed_revision differs from head_revision, and editable is true exactly when viewed_revision equals head_revision. A historical view is never editable, and a current-head view is the only view that may expose mutation actions.

The server binds each read, mutation candidate, and proposal card to the JSON-safe adapter_definition selected from the exact bound revision. Its record_types set exactly equals the record_definitions property-name set, and those definitions identify the fields, sections, required values, relationships, and connection states that candidates and cards may use. Mutation semantic validation uses that same revision-bound vocabulary; a client cannot replace it with an unrelated build-time definition or submit syntactically valid values outside it.

The campaign/revision-level creation context is read from the verified viewed revision and current head without looking up a record. It is returned only when viewed_revision equals head_revision and carries the campaign-wide editor_workflow_version required by editor_record_create_request, so creation remains available for an empty revision.
An edit or non-removal correction candidate preserves the bound record's record_type exactly. Record type migration is not an editor mutation and must fail closed before proposal creation.

source_changes contains exactly one server-produced source snapshot entry for every affected record subject in the diff card set: no missing, duplicate, or extra subject_record_id is permitted. Each entry's change_type and before/after nullability match the corresponding record mutation card: create is null-to-source, update is source-to-source, and delete is source-to-null. Each entry carries ownership: campaign, and each non-null snapshot parses to frontmatter, headings, fields, sections, and typed connections semantically equivalent to the corresponding structured before/after record or reference-resolution card. Name presence is derived from the revision-bound adapter_definition record_definitions[record_type].required_fields: when name is required, frontmatter name must match displayed_name; when name is not required, an omitted or blank name uses the record ID as displayed_name, matching the standalone/Atlas fallback. Each structured snapshot has exactly one top-level H1 matching displayed_name, including nameless record types. Source-to-record comparison is bidirectional: extra metadata keys or headings/sections are invalid, and normalized section bodies preserve internal blank lines. For reference-resolution cards, all non-connection content is unchanged with blank lines preserved and every resolution card for the subject contributes exactly one remove, retain, or redirect delta; unrelated connections remain intact.

operation_request.intent_digest must equal the request's top-level diff_digest. The action authorizes exactly the reviewed diff even though operation_request is excluded from the canonical payload projection.

Both action requests carry exact loaded proposal ID/version, revisions, workflow, payload/diff/validation digests, record bindings, impact, authority, and visibility values. operation_request.subject_id equals proposal.proposal_id, and operation_request.expected_revision and operation_request.expected_editor_workflow_version equal the top-level base revision and workflow values. For approval, the nested diff binding equals each top-level diff and confirmation duplicate exactly. The server compares current head and workflow before accepting the action. Approval additionally requires needs_review and passed validation with zero errors.

An accepted non-replay mutation consumes the supplied campaign-wide workflow version exactly once. A proposal returned from version N is stamped N+1; its approval or rejection consumes N+1 and completes at N+2. Exact replay, stale, and failed operations do not increment.

Every authority or visibility difference between a record card's before and after documents has one matching diff outcome, proposal outcome, and explicit approval confirmation ID. An outcome without a corresponding before/after transition is invalid.

Every ordinary connection card is derived from exactly one subject record before/after pair. The card set is the exact added, changed, and removed connection delta, so omissions, extras, no-ops, and directionally inconsistent cards fail closed. For a removal redirect, the reference_resolution card is the explicit exception: its before reference, after resolution, and derived_backlinks are the authoritative connection delta, and no duplicate record_updated or connection_updated card is required.

Record digests, property cards, connection and backlink cards, authority and visibility transition entries, affected_record_count, and approval confirmation sets are exact projections of one mutation. No field, section, connection, transition, card subject, or confirmation may be added, removed, or changed independently.

Every removal stage carries the exact impact binding and impact digest. The impact references, resolutions, resolution cards, affected record bindings, and derived backlink or connection effects form exact one-to-one logical mappings. Duplicate reference IDs, missing references, extra references, no-ops, self-redirects, and redirects to non-existent records fail closed.

A removal correction preserves the prior proposal provenance but reruns removal analysis against the explicitly bound current-head base revision. Its impact_binding and impact_digest identify that newly computed impact, and its resolutions cover that impact exactly; they need not equal the stale proposal's prior impact.
Staged warnings are carried into a passed proposal for review, but approval remains unavailable until the warning is removed; warnings are not implicitly acknowledged.

Typed incoming references are fail-closed by default: the server marks them permitted_unresolved=false, and the editor offers only removal or redirection unless a future adapter explicitly permits unresolved references.
